thread:
talia: Quick note—running mobile onboarding sampleapp with our new adaptive paginator and I see a stall when token rotation happens. Not a 429 from the server, but the client pipe collapses and UX on Android is notably worse than web. Anyone seen a mobile parity issue here?

omar: what SDKs/versions?

talia: android-sdk v1.3.0 (Kotlin), web-js 2.8.1. Repro: 12 parallel mobile clients scanning with pageSize=20, force token refresh ~6s in. Android clients drop concurrency to 1 and queue, web holds at 2-3.

ke: interesting. We tried to be conservative on mobile to avoid spiky battery/network use. Looks like mobile clamp is harsher. Logs (condensed):
[2026-04-05T18:02:10Z] fetchPage(client=9,page=4) -> 200 lat=140ms
[2026-04-05T18:02:16Z] auth:refresh(client=9) -> 200
[2026-04-05T18:02:16Z] android-sdk:concurrency.set(old=5,new=1,reason=auth_cycle)
[2026-04-05T18:02:16Z] enqueue(client=3,page=7) queued=9 wait=5.2s

talia: Web dropped to 2, mobile to 1. So UX on Android shows a 4-6s freeze.

omar: parity bug then. We should align clamp heuristics across SDKs but also consider mobile-specific defaults (less aggressive battery impact) — still, clamping to 1 on success is too severe.

ke: Agreed. Proposal: (A) unify clamp floor to max(2, ceil(old*0.25)) across all SDKs. (B) add a mobile-specific prefetchFactor lower bound (e.g., 0.8) so pump doesn't overshoot when slots shrink. (C) fast-path restore: if auth refresh returns 2xx and next 5 responses have <5% errors, ramp to previous window with jitter.

talia: +1. Also mobile network can have higher RTTs so the prefetch pump should be window-aware. Suggest prefetchTarget = clamp(1, ceil(currentSlots * prefetchFactor), maxPump) where prefetchFactor default 1.0 on mobile, 1.2 on web.

sre-bot: Observability note: adding metric "auth.clamp.trigger" with labels {sdk,old_window,new_window,reason}. Also capture prefetch.queue_depth at clamp time.

ke: Good call. That will let us confirm causality instead of guessing.

omar: Test plan: deterministic CI job that simulates token TTL boundary mid-scan for Android and Web, asserts mean queue time <2.5s and 95p <5s. We'll expose SDK_AUTH_CLAMP_PCT and SDK_PREFETCH_FACTOR env vars for experimentation.

talia: I'll prototype the Android change and add a small E2E harness that can run on emulator images in CI. Will also add a local debug switch to disable clamp for manual testing.

ci-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-13547 "sdk-mobile: align auth clamp + prefetch factors to avoid pagination pause". Linked logs and added test checklist.

ke: For rollout, let's gate behind env var for a week and run sampleapp load generator with both SDKs: https://ci.internal/redwood/sampleapp-load. Watch auth.clamp.trigger and prefetch.queue_depth. If green, flip default.

omar: Also note in onboarding doc: "Mobile clients may behave differently under token rotation; for heavy scans prefer refresh margin >30s or run with SDK_PREFETCH_FACTOR=1.0 to reduce pump overshoot."

talia: Thanks — will post PR link when I have the draft. If someone can review Android concurrency logic that'd help.

ke: I'll add a small patch for web parity and the observability instrumentation. Then we can coordinate rollout.

ci-bot: Reminder: add unit tests for pump scaling and a deterministic integration that manipulates time so CI isn't flaky.

talia: Great, thanks team. I'll follow up with PR + CI links. :rocket:
